title.zh: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标
title.en: Volume 247 Biographies 34: Peng Ershu, Lu Zhenfen, Yao Yanzhu, Bi Zhenji, Fang Guodong, Yu Pengju, Wang Tianjian, Yue Tingbiao
title.raw: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标

sentences.zh: =彭而述=彭而述，字子籛，河南鄧州人。

translations.literal: Peng Ershu, styled Ziliu, was a native of Dengzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ershu, courtesy name Ziliu, came from Dengzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官陽曲知縣，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, served as magistrate of Yangqu, and returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the jinshi examination in the Chongzhen era of the Ming and served as magistrate of Yangqu; when his mother died, he left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 順治初，英親王徇湖廣，薦為提學僉事，遷永州道參議。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying campaigned through Huguang, he was recommended as educational intendant and later transferred to assistant administrator of Yongzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi period, when the Prince of Ying led troops through Huguang, Peng was recommended as educational intendant and soon promoted to assistant administrator of Yongzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孔有德定湖南，薦而述授貴州巡撫，予兵三千以行。

translations.literal: When Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he recommended Ershu for appointment as governor of Guizhou and gave him three thousand troops for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: After Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he had Ershu appointed governor of Guizhou and supplied him with three thousand soldiers for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 次靖州，降將陳友龍叛，圍州城，而述夜開西門出，營山下，選勁騎乘霧衝陣，賊潰且走，副將賀進才戰死。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingzhou, the surrendered general Chen Youlong rebelled and besieged the prefectural city. Ershu opened the west gate at night and went out, encamped below the mountain, selected elite cavalry to charge through the fog, the rebels were routed and fled, and Vice-General He Jincai died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Near Jingzhou the surrendered general Chen Youlong rose in revolt and besieged the city. Ershu slipped out through the west gate by night, made camp below the hills, and sent picked cavalry charging through the mist; the rebels broke and fled, though Vice-General He Jincai was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 城兵大噪，欲與友龍合，而述拔眾退守寶慶，告有德益師，與賊相持紫陽河上。

translations.literal: The garrison troops made a great uproar, wishing to join Chen Youlong, but Ershu withdrew his forces to hold Baqing, reported to Youde to send more troops, and stalemate with the rebels along the Ziyang River.
translations.idiomatic: The city garrison clamored to join Chen Youlong, but Ershu pulled his men back to hold Baqing, asked Youde for reinforcements, and fought the enemy to a standstill on the Ziyang River.

sentences.zh: 永州陷，劾免官。

translations.literal: When Yongzhou fell, he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzhou fell he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂徵水西土司安坤，而述謀曰：「烏蒙、烏撒、鎮雄、東川四府與水西為脣齒，土司隴安籓又與安氏婚媾。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui campaigned against An Kun, the native chieftain of Shuixi, Ershu advised: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan are lip and teeth to Shuixi, and the native chieftain Long Anfan is also allied by marriage with the An clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui marched against An Kun, the Shuixi chieftain, Ershu counseled him: "Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan stand with Shuixi like lip and teeth, and the chieftain Long Anfan is tied to the An family by marriage as well.

sentences.zh: 今四府雖名內附，狼子野心，勢必顧惜其種類。

translations.literal: Though the four prefectures are now nominally submitted, they have the heart of a wolf cub and will surely look after their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: Although those four prefectures now profess allegiance, their hearts are wolfish; they are bound to protect their own people.

sentences.zh: 以水西之強，而安籓與四府附之，安坤未易制也。

translations.literal: With Shuixi's strength, and Anfan and the four prefectures supporting it, An Kun will not be easy to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuixi is strong, and with Anfan and the four prefectures behind it, An Kun will not be easily brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 莫如先定四府，馘安籓，然後西南可無患。」

translations.literal: It would be best first to secure the four prefectures and kill Anfan; then the southwest can be free of trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Better to secure the four prefectures first and eliminate Anfan; only then can the southwest be kept free of trouble."

sentences.zh: 三桂用其策，誅安坤。

translations.literal: Sangui adopted his plan and executed An Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui took his advice and put An Kun to death.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 三桂薦為雲南左布政使，而述乞歸，三桂留之，會有詔召，遂行，出會城三十里，一夕無疾卒。

translations.literal: Sangui recommended him as Left Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu begged to return home; Sangui detained him, but when an imperial summons arrived he set out, and thirty li beyond the provincial capital he died suddenly in a single night without prior illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui recommended him for Left Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu asked to retire, but Sangui kept him until an imperial summons came; he then departed, and thirty li outside the capital he died suddenly in the night without any known illness.

sentences.zh: =陸振芬=陸振芬，字令遠，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhenfen, styled Lingyuan, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfen, courtesy name Lingyuan, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 時兩粵未平，廷議破格用人，即新進士中遴才除道府。

translations.literal: At that time the two Guang provinces were not yet pacified; the court debated appointing men outside the usual rules and selecting talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural posts.
translations.idiomatic: The two Guang provinces were still unsettled, and the court decided to break with precedent by choosing talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural appointments.

sentences.zh: 振芬授廣東惠潮道副使，從師南征。

translations.literal: Zhenfen was appointed vice commissioner of the Huichao Circuit in Guangdong and followed the army south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen was made vice commissioner of Huichao Circuit in Guangdong and marched south with the expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 是冬，克南雄。

translations.literal: That winter they captured Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Nanxiong was taken.

sentences.zh: 七年春，度大庾嶺，次韶州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed the Dayu Range and halted at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed the Dayu Mountains and encamped at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 韶州以南望風降，進規會城，既下，振芬與總兵郭虎率師赴惠州，剿撫歸善、海豐諸寨。

translations.literal: South of Shaozhou all submitted at the news; they advanced on the provincial capital, and after it fell Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu led troops to Huizhou to suppress and pacify the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Everything south of Shaozhou surrendered at the first approach; after the provincial capital fell, Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu took forces to Huizhou to subdue and win over the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 將至，諸寨窺兵寡，出拒。

translations.literal: As they were about to arrive, the stockades saw that the troops were few and came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: As they drew near, the stockades, seeing how few troops they had, sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 振芬選精銳數百人繞出其旁擊之，獲一隊，諸寨皆懼。

translations.literal: Zhenfen selected several hundred elite troops to circle around and strike them from the flank, capturing one company, and all the stockades were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen picked several hundred crack troops to swing around and hit them from the flank, took one whole company prisoner, and every stockade was shaken.

sentences.zh: 於是諭以禍福，降者踵至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lectured them on gain and loss, and those who surrendered came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained the consequences they faced, and surrendering parties came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 至海豐，守者抗不下。

translations.literal: At Haifeng the defenders resisted and the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: At Haifeng the defenders held out and the place would not fall.

sentences.zh: 振芬與虎駐五坡驛，他將自羊氾嶺會師合攻之，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Zhenfen and Hu encamped at Wupo Post; other generals joined from Yangfan Ridge for a combined assault, and they then took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen and Hu camped at Wupo Post while other commanders converged from Yangfan Ridge for a joint attack, and the city was finally taken.

sentences.zh: 碣石衛亦降。

translations.literal: Jieshi Guard also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshi Guard surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 八年，抵潮州，上官，聯結諸鎮，檢制土官，招集流亡，簡省徭役，民始有更生之樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou and assumed office, linked the garrisons, restrained native officials, gathered the displaced, and reduced corvée levies, so the people at last knew the joy of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou and took up his post, coordinated the garrisons, kept native officials in check, brought back refugees, and cut back corvée burdens, until the people finally felt life returning.

sentences.zh: 亂甫定，用法嚴，郡縣輒濫禁無辜。

translations.literal: The turmoil had just subsided and the law was applied strictly; prefectures and counties often imprisoned the innocent without cause.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion only just ended, the law was enforced harshly and prefectures and counties often jailed innocent people at will.

sentences.zh: 振芬與屬吏約，期五十日清庶獄，囹圄為空。

translations.literal: Zhenfen agreed with his subordinates to clear the common prisons within fifty days, and the jails were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen pledged to his staff that they would clear the backlog of ordinary cases within fifty days, and the prisons were emptied.

sentences.zh: 九年，會師復平遠，總兵郝尚久故降將，陰持兩端，聞將改授水師副總兵，結山海諸寇僭立帥府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the armies reunited to recover Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, a former surrendered general, secretly wavered between two sides; hearing he was to be reassigned as vice commander of the naval forces, he joined the mountain and sea bandits in arrogating a commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year allied forces retook Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, once a Ming defector, had long hedged his loyalty; when he learned he was to be transferred to a naval vice command, he joined coastal and mountain rebels in setting up a rival headquarters.

sentences.zh: 振芬牒大吏策弭變，不應。

translations.literal: Zhenfen memorialized the high officials with a plan to quell the disturbance, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen sent the senior officials a memorial outlining how to head off the revolt, but they did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 十年春，尚久自署新泰侯，舉兵圍道署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu styled himself Marquis of Xintai and raised troops to besiege the circuit yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu declared himself Marquis of Xintai and marched on the circuit yamen.

sentences.zh: 振芬諭以大義，不從，使告變。

translations.literal: Zhenfen admonished him with the greater duty, but he would not listen, so Zhenfen sent word of the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen appealed to him on grounds of loyalty, but Shangjiu refused to listen, and Zhenfen sent word of the uprising.

sentences.zh: 秋，固山兵至，振芬約為內應，引外兵入，誅尚久。

translations.literal: In autumn the garrison troops arrived; Zhenfen had arranged to act from within, led the outside troops in, and executed Shangjiu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the banner garrison troops arrived; Zhenfen had arranged an inside response, admitted the relief force, and Shangjiu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 事平，引疾歸里。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he cited illness and retired to his home district.

sentences.zh: 家居四十年乃卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for forty years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for forty years before he died.

sentences.zh: =姚延著=姚延著，字象懸，浙江烏程人。

translations.literal: Yao Yanzhu, styled Xiangxuan, was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanzhu, courtesy name Xiangxuan, came from Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，除廣西慶遠知府。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 從師南征，調柳州，有守禦功，又調平樂。

translations.literal: He followed the army south, was transferred to Liuzhou where he had merit in defense, and was then transferred to Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south with the army, was posted to Liuzhou where he distinguished himself in defense, and was later moved to Pingle.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東嶺南道副使，撫僮寨，擢江南按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Lingnan Circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was elevated to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commissioner of Lingnan Circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was then promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鄭成功內犯，陷鎮江，入攻江寧。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong invaded inland, took Zhenjiang, and advanced to attack Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong raided inland, captured Zhenjiang, and pressed the attack on Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 延著佐總督郎廷佐繕守備，安輯危城，閭閻不擾。

translations.literal: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in preparing defenses, settled the endangered city, and the neighborhoods were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in organizing the defenses, steadied the besieged city, and kept the populace from panic.

sentences.zh: 民間時有羊尾黨，事發，株連數百人。

translations.literal: Among the people there was at times the Yangwei Party; when the affair broke, several hundred were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: A faction known as the Yangwei Party had appeared among the people; when the case broke, several hundred were dragged in.

sentences.zh: 延著謂廷佐曰：「寇在門，不可興大獄、搖人心。」

translations.literal: Yanzhu said to Tingzuo: "The enemy is at the gate; we must not launch a great prosecution and shake the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu told Tingzuo: "The enemy is at our gates—we cannot open a sweeping trial and unsettle the people."

sentences.zh: 獄乃解。

translations.literal: The case was then closed.
translations.idiomatic: The prosecution was dropped.

sentences.zh: 當事急，人多疑貳，民間有宿怨，輒誣以通敵。

translations.literal: At the crisis many were suspected of wavering; where old grudges existed among the people, they were often falsely accused of colluding with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the emergency many were suspected of disloyalty, and private feuds led to false charges of aiding the enemy.

sentences.zh: 延著嚴治反坐，多所全活。

translations.literal: Yanzhu strictly punished false accusation and thereby saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu cracked down hard on malicious prosecution and spared many innocent lives.

sentences.zh: 城民有升高而望者，邏者執之，總管喀喀木以為敵諜，延著力爭，得不死。

translations.literal: A townsman who climbed high to look about was seized by patrols; Commander Kekemu took him for an enemy spy, but Yanzhu argued strenuously and he was not put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols seized a townsman who had climbed up to look around; Commander Kekemu judged him a spy, but Yanzhu argued fiercely and the man was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木部兵擾城市，延著捕得械斃之。

translations.literal: Kekemu's troops harassed the city; Yanzhu captured them and had them executed by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Troops under Kekemu were harassing the city; Yanzhu arrested the offenders and had them strangled.

sentences.zh: 吏卒私掠被難婦女，延著親駐江乾，召其家，遣還者一千七百人，以此忤喀喀木。

translations.literal: Officials and soldiers privately seized women afflicted by the disaster; Yanzhu personally stationed himself on the riverbank, summoned their families, and sent back seventeen hundred persons, thereby offending Kekemu.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and soldiers were seizing women caught up in the turmoil; Yanzhu went in person to the riverbank, called their families forward, and restored seventeen hundred women to their homes—an act that put him at odds with Kekemu.

sentences.zh: 事定敘功，擢河南左布政使。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled merits were recorded and he was promoted to Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored his service was recognized and he was promoted to Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 旋以憂歸，而金壇獄起。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned home in mourning, and the Jintan case arose.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn a parent, and then the Jintan case erupted.

sentences.zh: 鎮江之陷也，屬縣戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Zhenjiang fell, the subordinate counties were placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenjiang fell, the surrounding counties were put on alert.

sentences.zh: 金壇知縣任體坤集縣中士大夫王重、袁大受等謀遣諸生十輩詣鎮江乞緩兵。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Jintan, Ren Tikun, gathered the local gentry Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to plan sending ten groups of students to Zhenjiang to plead for a truce.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan's magistrate Ren Tikun gathered local scholars Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to send ten parties of students to Zhenjiang to beg for a ceasefire.

sentences.zh: 丹徒亂民王再興兵起，復令書吏、耆民數十人送款，盡竊庫帑以遁。

translations.literal: The rebel Wang Zai of Dantu raised troops; Tikun again sent dozens of clerks and elders to submit, and they stole all the treasury funds and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dantu rebel Wang Zai rose in arms, Tikun again sent dozens of clerks and elders to offer submission—and they looted the treasury and fled.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木等擊敗成功，體坤乃復至縣，賂重、大受謁大吏，謂士民送款，冀掩棄城罪。

translations.literal: Kekemu and others defeated Chenggong; Tikun then returned to the county, bribed Chong and Dashou to visit the high officials, and claimed the gentry and people had submitted, hoping to cover his crime of abandoning the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Kekemu and the others routed Chenggong, Tikun returned to his post and bribed Chong and Dashou to lobby the senior officials, claiming the local elite had submitted in order to hide his own crime of deserting the county.

sentences.zh: 重、大受居鄉多不法，為諸生所撓。

translations.literal: Chong and Dashou had long committed many unlawful acts in their home districts and were thwarted by the students.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Dashou had long bullied their home districts, and the students had stood in their way.

sentences.zh: 至是欲以叛坐諸生，泄私怨，列姓名以上。

translations.literal: Now they wished to charge the students with rebellion to vent private grudges and submitted a list of names.
translations.idiomatic: They now sought to have the students convicted of treason to settle old scores and submitted a list of names.

sentences.zh: 巡按馬勝聲疏聞，下廷佐令延著鞫其獄。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Shengsheng memorialized the throne; the case was sent down to Tingzuo with orders for Yanzhu to try it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ma Shengsheng reported the matter to the throne; the case was referred to Tingzuo with orders for Yanzhu to hear it.

sentences.zh: 延著縶縣吏李鍾秀，訊得實，欲但坐體坤，餘皆減罪。

translations.literal: Yanzhu arrested the county clerk Li Zhongxiu, examined him and learned the truth, and wished to punish only Tikun while reducing the charges for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu arrested county clerk Li Zhongxiu, questioned him until the facts came out, and sought to punish only Tikun while leniency for the others.

sentences.zh: 大受騰書京師為蜚語，欲並陷延著，御史馮班發其狀。

translations.literal: Dashou sent letters to the capital spreading rumors, intending to implicate Yanzhu as well, but Censor Feng Ban exposed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou sent inflammatory letters to the capital hoping to drag Yanzhu down too, but Censor Feng Ban exposed what he was doing.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎尼滿奉詔勘提督馬逢知獄，命即訊，乃坐重、大受及諸士大夫集議者。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Niman was ordered by imperial edict to investigate the case of Governor-General Ma Fengzhi and was commanded to try this case at once; he convicted Chong, Dashou, and the gentry who had met in council.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Niman had been sent by imperial order to investigate Governor-General Ma Fengzhi's case and was told to try this one immediately; he convicted Chong, Dashou, and the scholars who had joined the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 諸生及書吏、耆民送款者皆斬，體坤以被逼迫減為絞。

translations.literal: The students and the clerks and elders who had submitted were all beheaded; Tikun, on the ground of coercion, had his sentence reduced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The students and every clerk and elder who had offered submission were beheaded; Tikun, as one who had acted under duress, was sentenced to strangulation instead.

sentences.zh: 巡按何可化又疏劾延著讞從叛罪人史記青、管得勝傅輕比，又有王天福、韓王錫並縱不擬罪，與金壇獄並論，亦坐絞。

translations.literal: Censor He Kehua again memorialized impeaching Yanzhu for leniently comparing the rebel criminals Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng Fu, and for releasing without sentence Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi; together with the Jintan case he too was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Kehua memorialized again, accusing Yanzhu of treating the rebels Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng Fu too lightly and of releasing Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi without punishment; lumped together with the Jintan affair, Yanzhu was also sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 時喀喀木主軍事，新破敵，尤威重，素不慊於延著。

translations.literal: At that time Kekemu controlled military affairs, had newly defeated the enemy, and was especially formidable; he had long been displeased with Yanzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Kekemu then held military authority, had just crushed the enemy, and wielded exceptional power; he had long borne a grudge against Yanzhu.

sentences.zh: 民間謂延著之死，喀喀木實主之。

translations.literal: Among the people it was said that Kekemu was in fact behind Yanzhu's death.
translations.idiomatic: Popular rumor held that Kekemu was really the one who brought about Yanzhu's death.

sentences.zh: 就刑日，江寧為罷市，士民哭踴。

translations.literal: On the day of execution Jiangning closed its markets; scholars and commoners wept and stamped in grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was executed Jiangning shut its markets; scholars and townspeople wept and stamped their feet in mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，數百里祭奠不絕，建祠雞鳴山下私祀焉。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, offerings continued without break for several hundred li, and a shrine was built below Jiming Hill for private worship.
translations.idiomatic: As his coffin was borne home, mourners offered sacrifices all along the route for hundreds of li, and a shrine was built below Jiming Hill where people worshipped him privately.

sentences.zh: 子淳燾，康熙六年進士，授內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Chunxi was a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunxi passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 伏闕上書為延著訟冤。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial to plead his father's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt at the palace gate and submitted a memorial pleading his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 累擢湖廣提學道僉事，坐事罷，未行，值叛卒夏逢龍之亂，誓死不為屈。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to educational intendant of Huguang Circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled he vowed to die rather than submit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to educational intendant of Huguang Circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled he swore he would die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 事聞，复官，授岳常澧道副使。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was restored to office and appointed vice commissioner of the Yuechangli Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his conduct was reported to the throne he was reinstated and appointed vice commissioner of Yuechangli Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =畢振姬=畢振姬，字亮四，山西高平人。

translations.literal: Bi Zhenji, styled Liangsi, was a native of Gaoping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhenji, courtesy name Liangsi, came from Gaoping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授平陽教授。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed professor at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed professor at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as an assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy and was promoted in stages to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy as assistant instructor and rose through the ranks to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 曹事暇，獨坐陋室，布被瓦盆，讀書不稍倦。

translations.literal: When official duties left him free, he sat alone in a humble room with cotton bedding and earthen bowls, reading without the slightest weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time from office he would sit alone in a plain room with cotton bedding and earthenware bowls, reading without ever tiring.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為山東濟南道參議。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of Jinan Circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was posted as assistant administrator of Jinan Circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，流民踞山谷為盜，振姬晝夜馳三百里往諭之，悉就撫，全活者七​​千餘人。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, displaced people occupied the mountain valleys as bandits; Zhenji rode day and night three hundred li to admonish them, and all submitted to pacification, saving more than seven thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year refugees had turned bandits in the mountain valleys; Zhenji rode three hundred li day and night to reason with them, and all came in to be pacified—more than seven thousand lives spared.

sentences.zh: 泰山香稅，歲羨餘七千金，例充公使錢，振姬悉以佐餉。

translations.literal: The incense tax of Mount Tai yielded a surplus of seven thousand taels yearly, which by rule went to official travel funds; Zhenji devoted it all to military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Tai incense tax produced an annual surplus of seven thousand taels, normally reserved for official travel expenses; Zhenji applied all of it to army rations.

sentences.zh: 調廣東驛傳道僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be intendant of the Post Relay Circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of the Post Relay Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時三籓使命往來絡繹，胥吏乘以私派折價，民苦之，振姬一繩以法，閱數月，減船數百，減​​費七萬有奇。

translations.literal: At that time the missions of the Three Feudatories came and went incessantly; clerks took the opportunity for private levies and discount extortion, and the people suffered. Zhenji applied the law uniformly; within several months he reduced boats by several hundred and cut costs by more than seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With the Three Feudatories' envoys constantly passing through, clerks imposed illegal surcharges and skimmed payments, to the people's misery. Zhenji enforced the law without favor; within months he cut several hundred boats from service and saved more than seventy thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道參政，擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of the Jinquyan Circuit in Zhejiang and promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to administrator of Jinquyan Circuit in Zhejiang and then promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 所至以廉能聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he won a reputation for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣布政使，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrative commissioner of Huguang and begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrative commissioner of Huguang, then asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，詔舉博學鴻儒，左都御史魏裔介、副都御史劉楗疏薦之。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign an edict called for recommending erudite scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign an edict summoned recommendations of learned scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian both memorialized in his favor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命廷臣舉清廉吏，裔介复疏言：「振姬清操絕世，才略過人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the court ordered officials to recommend incorrupt administrators; Yijie again memorialized: "Zhenji's integrity is unmatched in the age, and his talent and strategy surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court ordered officials to nominate incorrupt administrators; Yijie memorialized again: "Zhenji's integrity is unrivaled in our time, and his talent and strategic ability surpass ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 請告十餘年，躬耕百畝，讀書不輟。」

translations.literal: He has been on leave for more than ten years, personally tilling a hundred mu, and has never ceased reading."
translations.idiomatic: He has been retired for more than ten years, farming a hundred mu with his own hands, and has never stopped his studies."

sentences.zh: 楗亦言：「振姬居官不染一塵。

translations.literal: Jian also said: "In office Zhenji did not take a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also wrote: "In office Zhenji never soiled his hands with the slightest gain.

sentences.zh: 歸日一僕一馬，了無長物，真學行兼優之人。」

translations.literal: When he returned home he had but one servant and one horse and possessed nothing more—truly a man of combined learning and conduct."
translations.idiomatic: When he went home he had only one servant and one horse and owned nothing else—a man who truly united learning and character."

sentences.zh: 下部議，以振姬老，置勿用。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministries for deliberation; because Zhenji was old, he was set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and, on the ground of Zhenji's age, set the recommendation aside without appointing him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =方國棟=方國棟，字幹霄，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: Fang Guodong, styled Ganxiao, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guodong, courtesy name Ganxiao, came from Wanping in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 順治三年舉人，授蠡縣教諭。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor of Li County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed county instructor of Li.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累擢至刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered as an assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy and was promoted in stages to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy as assistant instructor and rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為廣東海北道僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out to serve as intendant of the Haibei Circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was posted as intendant of Haibei Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 海寇鄧耀居島中，時出剽掠。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Deng Yao lived on an island and often came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Deng Yao lived on an offshore island and raided the coast from time to time.

sentences.zh: 國棟以三千人分五道進剿，檄鄰道出兵扼要隘，擒耀，解散餘黨。

translations.literal: Guodong led three thousand men in five columns to suppress them, ordered neighboring circuits to send troops to hold the strategic passes, captured Yao, and dispersed the remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong took three thousand men in five columns against them, called on neighboring circuits to block the key passes, captured Yao, and broke up the remaining band.

sentences.zh: 事平，雷、廉兩部諸富人為賊所誣，械系者眾，國棟察其冤，為辨雪。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, many wealthy men of Lei and Lian prefectures had been falsely accused by the bandits and were shackled in large numbers; Guodong saw their innocence and cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, many wealthy men in Lei and Lian prefectures had been framed by the pirates and thrown in chains; Guodong found them innocent and secured their release.

sentences.zh: 諸富人裒千金為報，國棟曰：「吾憫若無辜，柰何污我？」

translations.literal: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels as a reward; Guodong said: "I pitied your innocence—why would you try to stain me?"
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels to thank him; Guodong said, "I pitied your innocence—why would you try to bribe me?"

sentences.zh: 卻之。

translations.literal: He refused it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 遷山西寧武道參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be assistant administrator of Ningwu Circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant administrator of Ningwu Circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年裁缺，改江南蘇松常道參議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi his post was abolished; he was reassigned as assistant administrator of the Susongchang Circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was abolished in the sixth year of Kangxi, he was reassigned as assistant administrator of Susongchang Circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 太湖堤岸傾圮，率吏民修葺，修沿海墩台及吳淞、劉河兩徬，工費不擾民。

translations.literal: The dikes on Lake Tai collapsed; he led officials and people to repair them, restored coastal watch towers and the two embankments of Wusong and Liuhe, and the work costs did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lake Tai dikes gave way, he led officials and commoners in repairs, rebuilt coastal watch towers and the Wusong and Liuhe embankments, and kept the labor levies from burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 師下閩、粵，徵調旁午，國棟一意與民休息，每遇急徵，從容部署。

translations.literal: When the army descended on Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions came in rapid succession; Guodong was wholly intent on letting the people rest, and whenever urgent levies arrived he deployed resources calmly.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces marched into Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions poured in without pause; Guodong was determined to give the people respite, and whenever urgent demands arrived he met them with calm planning.

sentences.zh: 芻茭糧糗，預儲以待，軍興無乏，閭左晏然。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain rations were stored in advance to await need; when the army mobilized nothing was lacking, and the neighborhoods were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled fodder and grain ahead of time so that when troops mobilized nothing ran short, and the common people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 戒屬吏無朘民，郡縣稍稍知斂戢，不敢事剝削。

translations.literal: He admonished subordinates not to squeeze the people; prefectures and counties gradually learned restraint and dared not practice extortion.
translations.idiomatic: He warned his staff against squeezing the people, and prefectures and counties gradually learned to restrain themselves and ceased their extortions.

sentences.zh: 連歲用兵，度支不給，詔各省籌裕餉之策。

translations.literal: War continued year after year and the treasury could not meet expenses; an edict ordered each province to devise plans for adequate military funds.
translations.idiomatic: Years of warfare had drained the treasury, and an edict ordered every province to propose ways to secure adequate military funds.

sentences.zh: 國棟言：「古今生財之說，開與節二者而已。

translations.literal: Guodong said: "Throughout history theories of generating wealth come down to only two things: opening sources and economizing.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong wrote: "Throughout history, raising revenue has come down to only two things: finding new sources and cutting expenses.

sentences.zh: 議開於今日，已無可加，當議節，自朝廷始。

translations.literal: To discuss opening sources today, there is nothing more to add; we should discuss economizing, beginning with the court itself.
translations.idiomatic: As for opening new sources today, there is little left to do; we should economize, and that must begin at court.

sentences.zh: 舊制，江南歲市布五萬匹供宮府賚予，宜可罷，歲省帑金三萬。」

translations.literal: By old regulation Jiangnan yearly markets fifty thousand bolts of cloth for palace grants; this should be abolished, saving thirty thousand taels from the treasury each year."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules Jiangnan supplies fifty thousand bolts of cloth yearly for palace gifts; that practice should end, saving thirty thousand taels a year."

sentences.zh: 議上，報可，滿洲兵駐防蘇州，議築營舍於王府基，當城中。

translations.literal: The proposal was submitted and approved. Manchu troops garrisoned Suzhou; it was proposed to build barracks on the old princely mansion site in the center of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved. When Manchu troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, officials proposed building barracks on the old princely mansion site in the heart of the city.

sentences.zh: 國棟以兵民雜居難久安，持不可，乃改營南城隙地，民便之。

translations.literal: Guodong held that soldiers and civilians living mixed could not long remain stable and firmly opposed it; barracks were then placed on vacant land in the southern city, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong argued that soldiers and civilians could not live mixed together in stability and firmly opposed the plan; the barracks were moved to open ground in the southern city instead, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 宜興善權山中寺僧與豪族爭地，聚眾焚寺殺僧，知縣告亂，大吏將發兵。

translations.literal: At Shanchansi in Shanquan, Yixing, monks disputed land with powerful clans; they gathered a mob, burned the temple, and killed monks. The magistrate reported rebellion and high officials were about to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanchansi in Shanquan, Yixing, monks were locked in a land dispute with powerful families; a mob burned the temple and killed monks. The magistrate reported an uprising and senior officials prepared to send troops.

sentences.zh: 國棟單騎馳往，得首禍寘法，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Guodong rode alone in haste to the scene, seized the ringleaders and punished them by law, and questioned no one else.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong rode out alone, arrested the ringleaders and punished them under the law, and pressed no further inquiries.

sentences.zh: 吳俗健訟，喜投缿告密，國棟輒不問，即有所案，亦從寬。

translations.literal: Wu custom was fond of litigation and delighted in dropping accusations into the complaint box; Guodong routinely paid no heed, and even when there were cases he was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu were litigious and fond of anonymous denunciations; Guodong generally ignored them, and even when he took up a case he dealt leniently.

sentences.zh: 馭吏嚴，而拊循士民具有恩意。

translations.literal: He was strict with subordinates, yet in comforting scholars and commoners he showed real kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was strict with his staff yet treated scholars and townspeople with genuine kindness.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 吳民思之，建祠虎丘山麓以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill in his memory.

sentences.zh: =於朋舉=於朋舉，字襄子，江南金壇人。

translations.literal: Yu Pengju, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Jintan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pengju, courtesy name Xiangzi, came from Jintan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and upon completing his training was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為河南睢陳道副使，政不擾民。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as vice commissioner of the Suichen Circuit in Henan; his administration did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as vice commissioner of Suichen Circuit in Henan, governing without harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 郾城盜殺縣官而逸，士民洶洶，謂城將受屠。

translations.literal: At Yancheng bandits killed the county magistrate and fled; gentry and people were in uproar, saying the city would be massacred.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits at Yancheng killed the county magistrate and escaped; the townspeople panicked, fearing the city would be put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 朋舉馳至，撫諭毋恐。

translations.literal: Pengju hurried there and comforted them, telling them not to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju rode there at once, reassured the people, and told them not to be afraid.

sentences.zh: 營將以兵至，拒不使入城。

translations.literal: A garrison commander was bringing troops; Pengju refused to let them enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: When a garrison commander marched up with troops, Pengju refused to let them enter the city.

sentences.zh: 大吏召朋舉詰責，對曰：「郾城令，朋舉婦翁也。

translations.literal: A high official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he replied: "The magistrate of Yancheng is Pengju's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: A senior official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he answered: "The magistrate of Yancheng is my wife's father.

sentences.zh: 豈不欲甘心是盜？

translations.literal: Would I not wish to take satisfaction on those bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I would not want those bandits punished?

sentences.zh: 獨柰何苦良民！」

translations.literal: Only why must innocent people suffer!"
translations.idiomatic: But why should innocent people suffer for it!"

sentences.zh: 大吏悟，止兵，亦得盜正其罪。

translations.literal: The high official understood, halted the troops, and the bandits were also brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: The senior official understood, held back the troops, and the bandits were still brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 遷福建福寧道參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of Funing Circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrator of Funing Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 興化瀕海，鎮將所部皆群盜受撫者。

translations.literal: Xinghua bordered the sea; the troops under the regional commander were all bandit gangs who had submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua lay on the coast; the regional commander's troops were all former bandits who had accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 有材官辱張氏僕，張氏以告。

translations.literal: An officer insulted a servant of the Zhang family, and the Zhangs reported it.
translations.idiomatic: An officer humiliated a servant of the Zhang family, and the Zhangs lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 鎮將撻材官，部卒大譁，毀張氏之室，欲劫鎮將為亂。

translations.literal: The commander flogged the officer; the troops made a great uproar, wrecked the Zhang residence, and wished to seize the commander and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had the officer flogged; his men mutinied, wrecked the Zhang house, and tried to seize their commander and rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 鎮將避去，則縊被撻者寘張氏，謂其僕殺之。

translations.literal: The commander fled; they then hanged the man who had been flogged and placed the body at the Zhangs', claiming their servant had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The commander fled; the mutineers hanged the flogged man and left the body at the Zhangs' door, claiming their servant had murdered him.

sentences.zh: 朋舉甫到官，廉得首惡，猝縛至，集文武吏會鞫，健兒帶刀環立瞋視。

translations.literal: Pengju had just taken office; he investigated and found the ringleaders, suddenly bound them and brought them in, gathered civil and military officials for joint trial, while braves with swords stood glaring in a ring.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju had just taken office; he traced the ringleaders, had them seized at once, and convened civil and military officials for a joint hearing while armed braves ringed the hall glaring.

sentences.zh: 朋舉從容曰：「若曹幹軍法，罪重。

translations.literal: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law; the crime is grave.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law—a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 念若曹約束無素，但用殺人律，罪有專屬。」

translations.literal: Considering that you have never been disciplined, we will apply only the statute on homicide; the crime has its proper bearer."
translations.idiomatic: Since you have never been properly disciplined, we will apply only the statute on homicide—the guilty party must be identified."

sentences.zh: 眾乃泥首，言殺人者為張氏僕。

translations.literal: The crowd then pressed their foreheads to the ground and said the killer was the Zhangs' servant.
translations.idiomatic: The men then kowtowed and claimed the killer was the Zhangs' servant.

sentences.zh: 朋舉曰：「若曹氣焰何等，彼能於千百健兒中奪一人縊之耶？」

translations.literal: Pengju said: "What sort of spirit do you have—could he seize one man among a thousand braves and hang him?"
translations.idiomatic: Pengju said: "With your swagger, could a mere servant seize one of you among a thousand armed men and hang him?"

sentences.zh: 召訊證者，俱吐實，誅三人而事定。

translations.literal: He summoned witnesses for questioning; all told the truth, three were executed, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He called witnesses; all confessed, three were executed, and the matter was closed.

sentences.zh: 泉州提督剿海盜，盜逸入興化界，鎮將獲數百人。

translations.literal: The Quanzhou provincial admiral suppressed sea pirates; the pirates fled into Xinghua territory and the regional commander captured several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial admiral of Quanzhou pursued sea pirates; the pirates fled into Xinghua and the regional commander seized several hundred.

sentences.zh: 朋舉視其嘗薙發者，曰：「此良民被陷，當宥。」

translations.literal: Pengju looked at those who had once tonsured their hair and said: "These are innocent people who were trapped; they should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing those who had once shaved their heads in the Ming style, Pengju said: "These are innocent people caught up in the affair—they should be spared."

sentences.zh: 有年少者，曰：「童穉何知，又當宥。」

translations.literal: Among them were youths; he said: "What do children know—they too should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Among them were youths; he said: "Children know nothing of this—they too should be spared."

sentences.zh: 全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Very many were thus spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: A great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功屯廈門，與漳州隔海相望。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong was stationed at Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the strait.

sentences.zh: 固山額真駐會城，遣兵戍漳州，番代歲四易，民苦供役。

translations.literal: The garrison commander was stationed at the provincial capital and sent troops to garrison Zhangzhou; rotations changed four times a year, and the people suffered from supplying corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander at the provincial capital sent troops to hold Zhangzhou; reliefs rotated four times a year, and the people groaned under the levies.

sentences.zh: 朋舉請駐防無屢更，不許；

translations.literal: Pengju requested that the garrison not be changed so often; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju asked that the garrison not be rotated so frequently; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 固請展其期，歲再易，民稍蘇息。

translations.literal: He firmly petitioned to extend the term; rotations came twice a year, and the people found some relief.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard to lengthen the rotation interval to twice a year, and the people gained some respite.

sentences.zh: 擢四川按察使、山東右布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and right administrative commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and Right Administrative Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起授湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed administrative commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to service as administrative commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 上官，見胥吏至數百，曰：「兵初罷，民方重困。

translations.literal: Upon assuming office he saw clerks numbering in the hundreds and said: "The troops have only just stood down and the people are in deep distress.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he found hundreds of clerks and said: "The armies have only just stood down and the people are in deep distress.

sentences.zh: 此曹鮮衣美食，縱橫市井間，何所​​取諸？」

translations.literal: These fellows dress in fine clothes and eat well, swaggering through the markets—where do they get it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet these men dress well, eat well, and swagger through the markets—where does it all come from?"

sentences.zh: 汰其十九，擇謹願者，取足供文書而已。

translations.literal: He dismissed nineteen out of twenty, chose the prudent and willing, and kept only enough to handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed nine out of ten, kept only the prudent and dutiful, and retained just enough staff to handle paperwork.

sentences.zh: 數為大吏言地方利病，有司賢不肖積與之忤，被劾鐫級，未行，而大吏以貪敗。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told high officials of local benefits and harms; officials worthy and unworthy alike accumulated grievances against him; he was impeached and demoted in rank, and before he could leave the senior official was ruined for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported local abuses to senior officials; worthy and unworthy magistrates alike resented him; he was impeached and demoted, and before he could depart the senior official himself was ruined for corruption.

sentences.zh: 士民惜之。

translations.literal: Gentry and people regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =王天鑑=王天鑑，字近微，直隸萬全人。

translations.literal: Wang Tianjian, styled Jinwei, was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tianjian, courtesy name Jinwei, came from Wanquan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授山東恩縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 縣接直隸界，自明季為盜藪，嘗一歲七被寇。

translations.literal: The county bordered Zhili; since the late Ming it had been a bandit haunt and once suffered seven raids in a single year.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered Zhili and had been a bandit haunt since the late Ming; one year it was raided seven times.

sentences.zh: 天鑑上官，諭父老曰：「往歲寇至，縣輒不守，由人無固志。

translations.literal: When Tianjian took office he told the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county always failed to hold, because people had no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Tianjian told the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county always fell because the people had no firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 自今勿復逃，視知縣所向。」

translations.literal: From now on do not flee again; watch where the magistrate goes."
translations.idiomatic: From now on do not flee—watch where your magistrate goes."

sentences.zh: 俄而寇大至，天鑑坐城上，從容指揮，寇疑有伏，逡巡去。

translations.literal: Soon bandits came in force; Tianjian sat on the wall and directed affairs calmly; the bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a large band arrived; Tianjian sat on the wall and directed the defense calmly; the bandits suspected a trap and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是葺樓櫓，治城隍，嚴候望，時巡徼，守具大備。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired towers and battlements, restored the city moat, tightened watch and signal posts, patrolled regularly, and defenses were fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired towers and battlements, restored the moat, tightened watch posts, patrolled regularly, and made the defenses complete.

sentences.zh: 按行鄉鄙，舉團練，立砦十有九，枹鼓相聞，久之得步卒萬八千、騎士三百。

translations.literal: He toured the countryside, raised militia, established nineteen stockades with drums and gongs within hearing of one another, and in time mustered eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the countryside, organized militia, and established nineteen stockades whose drums could be heard from one to the next; in time he fielded eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史疏聞，令天鑑自治兵。

translations.literal: The touring censor memorialized the throne, and Tianjian was ordered to command troops himself.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor reported to the throne, and Tianjian was authorized to command troops in his own right.

sentences.zh: 廉得境內賊渠數輩，夜突至其鄉呼之出，賊錯愕不能遁，皆誅之。

translations.literal: He investigated and found several bandit chiefs within the district; by night he suddenly appeared in their villages and called them out; the bandits were startled and could not escape—all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He traced several bandit chiefs in the district, raided their villages by night, and called them out; caught off guard, they could not escape and were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 寇據曹縣，巡撫檄天鑑與諸道兵會剿，率所部為前鋒，冒矢石深入，諸軍踵之，復其城。

translations.literal: Bandits held Cao County; the governor ordered Tianjian and troops from several circuits to join in suppression; he led his own forces as vanguard, braved arrows and stones in deep advance, the armies followed, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized Cao County, the governor ordered Tianjian and allied forces to join the campaign; he led his men as vanguard, pushed through arrow and stone fire, the main force followed, and the city was retaken.

sentences.zh: 嘗以輕騎逐賊，日暮被圍，短兵相接，手格殺數賊，潰圍出，不失一騎。

translations.literal: Once with light cavalry he pursued bandits; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand to hand, personally killed several bandits, broke out of the encirclement, and lost not a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Once he pursued bandits with a light cavalry detachment; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand to hand, killed several with his own blade, broke out, and did not lose a single horse.

sentences.zh: 在恩四年，屢與寇戰，俘馘無算，降者安撫之。

translations.literal: In four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and pacified those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and settled those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 寇遠遁，招徠屯種，流亡復歸，墾荒千八百頃。

translations.literal: When bandits fled far away he summoned people to settle and farm; refugees returned, and eighteen hundred qing of wasteland were brought under cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits fled he encouraged resettlement and farming; refugees returned and eighteen hundred qing of wasteland were reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 建書院，弦誦不輟。

translations.literal: He built an academy where study and recitation never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy where students studied without interruption.

sentences.zh: 政聲為山東最，上考，內遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: His administrative reputation was the finest in Shandong; on superior evaluation he was transferred within the capital to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was the finest in Shandong; rated at the top of his evaluation he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，始行耤田親耕禮，天鑑參酌古今，悉合禮宜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field was first performed; Tianjian drew on ancient and modern precedents and all conformed to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor first performed the sacred-field plowing rite; Tianjian drew on ancient and modern precedents and arranged everything in proper ritual form.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director.

sentences.zh: 主山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為陝西河西道參議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of Hexi Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as assistant administrator of Hexi Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與屬吏約，毋獵民枉法。

translations.literal: He agreed with subordinates not to hunt the people or bend the law.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged to his staff that they would not prey on the people or pervert the law.

sentences.zh: 天鑑固長治兵，按籍討軍實，誡將弁毋以軍糈肥私橐。

translations.literal: Tianjian was by nature skilled at governing troops; he checked registers to verify military strength and admonished officers not to fatten private purses with army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian was a natural commander; he audited registers to verify troop strength and warned officers against lining their pockets with army grain.

sentences.zh: 性剛介負氣，數忤上官。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and proud; he often offended superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and unyielding by nature, he often clashed with his superiors.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，謝病歸。

translations.literal: After little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 絕跡公府，門下士或有餽遺，不受，曰：「飭簠簋，惜名節，足以報舉主矣！」

translations.literal: He vanished from public offices; when disciples sometimes offered gifts he would not accept them, saying: "To keep my vessels in order and cherish my reputation is enough to repay those who recommended me!"
translations.idiomatic: He kept away from official circles; when disciples offered gifts he refused them, saying: "Keeping my conduct clean and my name intact is repayment enough to those who recommended me!"

sentences.zh: 康熙初，大臣薦，不出。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign ministers recommended him, but he would not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign ministers recommended him, but he would not return to office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =趙廷標=趙廷標，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingbiao was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingbiao came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，以拔貢生授福建永定知縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian as a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 廣東大埔逸寇江龍以萬餘人犯縣城，廷標城守。

translations.literal: The fugitive bandit Jiang Long of Dapu in Guangdong invaded the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao defended the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw Jiang Long of Dapu, Guangdong, attacked the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao held the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇穴地入，瀦池水以待，地砲不得發；

translations.literal: The bandits burrowed underground; he dammed the moat to hold water so land mines could not be fired.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tunneled in; he dammed the moat to flood the approaches so land mines could not be detonated.

sentences.zh: 樹雲梯乘城，於城上懸柵墮之。

translations.literal: They raised cloud ladders to scale the wall; he hung barriers above the wall to drop on them.
translations.idiomatic: They raised siege ladders; he hung barriers along the parapet to drop on them.

sentences.zh: 持三月，食垂盡。

translations.literal: The siege lasted three months and food was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three months until food was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 值立春，廷標張鼓樂，開城門，迎春東郊。

translations.literal: When the Beginning of Spring arrived, Tingbiao set out drums and music, opened the city gate, and welcomed spring in the eastern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Beginning of Spring festival Tingbiao staged music, opened the gates, and led the spring rites in the eastern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 寇疑有伏，引去。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suspected a trap and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 密遣兵間道往伏兩山間，出不意夾擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent troops by hidden paths to lie in ambush between two mountains and struck them unexpectedly from both sides, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent troops by hidden paths to ambush them between two hills and struck from both sides by surprise, routing them.

sentences.zh: 進至龍磜寨，捕斬略盡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Longji Stockade, he captured and beheaded nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Longji Stockade and captured or killed nearly all who remained.

sentences.zh: 擢湖廣衡州同知，署府事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted in prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted as prefect.

sentences.zh: 蠲賦墾荒，流亡復業。

translations.literal: He remitted taxes and opened wasteland; refugees returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted taxes, encouraged reclamation, and brought refugees back to their farms.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，賑恤有實惠。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine his relief brought real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine his relief reached those who needed it.

sentences.zh: 經略大學士洪承疇薦廷標，十七年，擢雲南迤東道副使。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, commissioner-general, recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of Yidong Circuit in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of Yidong Circuit in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 安普諸番為土官所誘，競作不靖。

translations.literal: The tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, vied in making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, rose in unrest one after another.

sentences.zh: 廷標設方略、行間，解散之，遂復維摩舊地。

translations.literal: Tingbiao devised strategy and used agents among them to disperse them, and thereby recovered the old territory of Weimo.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao devised strategy and used agents to break them up, and thereby recovered the old Weimo territory.

sentences.zh: 移檄諭寧州彌勒、巴盤、八甸，罷捕逐之令，令諸持田器者皆為良民，持兵者乃為賊。

translations.literal: He sent proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, abolishing orders to hunt and drive people out, decreeing that all who held farming tools were good people and only those who held weapons were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, ending the orders to hunt people down, and ruled that anyone holding farm tools was a law-abiding subject while only those bearing arms were bandits.

sentences.zh: 巡行安撫，諸路悉平。

translations.literal: He toured to pacify and comfort; all routes were entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the region to reassure the people, and every route was pacified.

sentences.zh: 治迤東十八年。

translations.literal: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，調廣東廣肇南韶道副使。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Guangzhaonanxiao Circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of Guangzhaonanxiao Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 安普民、蠻聞其去，塹道塞城留之。

translations.literal: When the people and tribes of Anpu heard he was leaving, they dug ditches and blocked the city to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people and tribes of Anpu learned he was leaving, they dug trenches and blocked the gates to keep him from going.

sentences.zh: 慰諭再三，乃得行。

translations.literal: After repeated consolation and instruction he was able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Only after repeated reassurances was he able to leave.

sentences.zh: 兩粵八排諸山寇聞廷標來，望風解散。

translations.literal: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they dispersed at the news.
translations.idiomatic: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they melted away at the news.

sentences.zh: 連州亂，至，立就撫。

translations.literal: Lianzhou was in revolt; when he arrived they immediately submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Lianzhou was in revolt; when he arrived the rebels submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 逾年以憂去。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he left office to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 起湖南驛鹽道副使。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of the Post and Salt Circuit in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice commissioner of the Post and Salt Circuit in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 捕治劇寇，誅其渠，餘悉縱歸農。

translations.literal: He captured and punished fierce bandits, executed their leaders, and released the rest to return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: He captured major bandits, executed their leaders, and sent the rest back to their farms.

sentences.zh: 湖南方用兵，芻茭械仗，儲峙供給，不誤晷刻，民不困役。

translations.literal: Hunan was then at war; fodder, weapons, and stores were supplied without missing a moment, and the people were not worn down by corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was at war; he supplied fodder, arms, and stores without a moment's delay, and kept corvée burdens from crushing the people.

sentences.zh: 兼攝糧道。

translations.literal: He also acted as grain intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 會湘東民變，巡撫韓世琦令廷標往撫之。

translations.literal: When the people of eastern Hunan rose in disturbance, Governor Han Shiqi ordered Tingbiao to go pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Hunan erupted in unrest, Governor Han Shiqi sent Tingbiao to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 單騎馳諭，皆悔泣聽命，散遣之。

translations.literal: He rode alone in haste to instruct them; all repented, wept, and obeyed, and he dispersed them.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone to reason with them; they wept, repented, and obeyed, and he sent them home.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，修岳麓書院，置田禀諸生。

translations.literal: When affairs were somewhat settled he restored Yuelu Academy and set aside fields to support students.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned he restored Yuelu Academy and endowed fields to support its students.

sentences.zh: 嘗行部至衡州，父老羅拜車下，號以「慈母」。

translations.literal: Once when touring his circuit he reached Hengzhou; elders bowed in rows beneath his carriage and hailed him as "a loving mother."
translations.idiomatic: Once on circuit he reached Hengzhou; elders lined up to bow before his carriage and called him "the loving mother."

sentences.zh: 俄遷陝西糧儲道參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be assistant administrator of the Grain Storage Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to assistant administrator of the Grain Storage Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 已病，值武昌兵變，軍書至，猶強起視事。

translations.literal: He was already ill; when the military mutiny at Wuchang broke out and dispatches arrived, he still forced himself up to attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: He was already ill; when troops mutinied at Wuchang and dispatches arrived, he still dragged himself to his desk.

sentences.zh: 病篤乞歸，至家卒。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave and he begged to return home; he died upon reaching home.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened and he begged to go home; he died as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：自置督撫，而兩司權輕，況於各道；

translations.literal: The commentary says: Since governors-general and governors were established, the two provincial commissioners grew lighter in authority, and still more the circuit intendant posts.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Once governors-general and governors were established, the authority of the two provincial commissioners grew lighter—and the circuit posts lighter still.

sentences.zh: 然以賢者處之，奉職循理，視民之所急，弭亂解嬈，亦足以為治。

translations.literal: Yet when the worthy hold such posts, fulfilling duty and following principle, looking to what the people urgently need, quelling disorder and relieving distress, that is also enough for good government.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when worthy men hold these posts, perform their duties faithfully, heed what the people urgently need, and quell disorder and ease hardship, that too is government enough.

sentences.zh: 而述、振芬、振姬、天鑑皆有才略，根本尤在廉勤。

translations.literal: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategy; the root lay especially in integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategic ability; above all they were rooted in integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 延著、國棟、廷標當治亂用重之日，濟之以寬仁，雖以是罷貶，甚或中危法，而一不自卹，是皆能舉其職者。

translations.literal: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served in days when order and disorder called for stern measures; they supplemented this with leniency and kindness. Though some were dismissed or demoted for it, and some even fell under grave law, none spared themselves—these all were men who could fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served when governing turmoil demanded stern measures, yet they tempered authority with mercy. Some were dismissed or demoted for it, and some even faced capital charges, but none thought of themselves—these were men who truly did their duty.

sentences.zh: 澤及於斯民，亦已多矣。

translations.literal: The blessings that reached these people were already very great.
translations.idiomatic: The good they did for the people was already very great indeed.
